slides.title: Perpendicular means ==flip it and flip the sign==

slides.stem: The line $2x + 6y = 18$ is graphed in the $xy$-plane. Which equation represents a line that is perpendicular to it and passes through the point $(4, -2)$?

slides.body: From $Ax + By = C$, the slope is $-\frac{A}{B} = -\frac{2}{6} = -\frac{1}{3}$. Perpendicular flips and negates: slope $3$. Through $(4, -2)$: $-2 = 3(4) + b$, so $b = -14$ and the line is $y = 3x - 14$. Choice B is what you get if you keep $-\frac{1}{3}$ — a parallel line through the same point.

slides.title: Slope straight from standard form
slides.body:
For $Ax + By = C$, the slope is $-\frac{A}{B}$. Read it off; never waste time rearranging.

Then check what the question wants: parallel keeps the slope, perpendicular flips the fraction and the sign. The wrong one is always in the choices.
